answer: One concrete defense is to bind each identity to a scarce, rivalrous root that a single operator cannot cheaply duplicate, such as a hardware attestation or a verified human check. Like saffron, genuine roots are costly because each demands real harvest; and like a lotus, only one blooms per rooted stalk. An attacker can still conjure an ocean of names, but without distinct roots they collapse into one trusted unit, so flooding the registry earns no extra votes.
